title: the stands that measure the claims of the tree and the life
intent: The wave repairs four defects of the evidence of the package of the waves 101 to 103, and all four were found by the discriminator of that package (docs/PLAN.md section 16.100).  (1) **F48.** The promise of the claim of the wave 101 -- "the socket of a zombie owner is swept away and a zombie owner is not adopted as if it lived" -- was a consequence, not a form of code, and no stand measured it.  The wave adds a stand of the behaviour of `lib/yeah-life.el' to the check of the wave 101: it replaces the reader of the state of a process with a table of the stand and asks the kernel itself.  (2) **F51.** The two promises of the claim of the wave 102 -- "the tree is read once for a list of the descendants" and "the tree is stopped as a whole" -- were not measured either.  The wave adds three stands to the shell check of the wave 102 and measures both values from outside, through the existing seam `PROC_ROOT', without touching `scripts/lib/tree.sh'.  (3) **F52.** The falsifier of the claim of the wave 101 says that *another file of the repository* defines the rule of the life of a process beside it, and the sentinel of that assertion read two directories and knew the rule only by the form of its name.  The wave widens the sentinel to the whole tree and adds a second recognition, the sign of a rule.  (4) **F53.** The guard of the documentation read `docs/*.md', `AGENTS.md', `README.md' and `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md' -- and not `waves/*.json', where the records of the waves live (the section 16.99 says so outright).  The wave makes the guard read the records as well, and it says what the rule of the file does to them: nothing, because a record is a document of the past.
objection: The wave touches no kernel, and its price is named.  (a) **The stand of F51 measures the arrival of a signal, not the death of a process.**  The death of a process is the rule of the life of a process itself, and that rule belongs to the kernel, in one place, and not to a stand.  (b) **The rule "the stat file of a process is read by one module" stays in `lib/'.**  The check of the wave 100 that reads the stat file is F47 and not F52, and its file is not this wave's; the widening of that rule to the whole tree would touch the check of the wave 100 and would enlarge this wave into a foreign finding.  (c) **The promise of the claim of the documentation was narrower than its measurement.**  The scope of the claim did not hold `waves/', and the guard was stricter than the promise; the parent amended the claim on 2026-11-21 (the text, the falsifier and the scope) and the reason is recorded in the section 16.104.  (d) **The rule of the file does not apply to the records, and the price of that is two names.**  If the rule were applied to the records -- and nothing else were changed -- the guard would find **two** names of files that are not on disk: `tests/support/yeah-proc.el' in `waves/wave-101.json' (the module before it moved to `lib/yeah-proc.el') and `sessions/...' in `waves/wave-64.json' (a shortened name, and the record says so itself).  **The price was seven names until 2026-11-21, and that was a measurement with the rule of the ignored paths taken away as well:** the guard asks git about the ignored names *before* it asks whether the document is a record, so the other five names the records hold (`bench/results', `tests/artifacts' and `bench/results/20261115T150251Z.jsonl' in `waves/wave-63.json' -- the output of a run, which git ignores) are silent already, and the same rule is silent about eleven names in `docs/PLAN.md'.  Seven is the number of names the records hold, not the number of refusals the guard would give.  None of the seven is a defect of today, and none of them is repaired by this wave: the records of the waves do not belong to it, and the decision whether the rule of the file applies to them is the owner's.  (e) **The guard of the documentation reads the records whole.**  Measured: 702 ms becomes 744 ms (+42 ms) -- a snapshot of 2026-11-21, on a tree of 108 records; the tree whose guard did not read the records is gone, and the difference cannot be measured again.  The measurements are current: the records are 110 today, 667 KB of text, and they are read whole, and so they are meant to be.  (f) **The live route was not checked.**  The wave touches no code of the kernel and only the evidence of the package.  (g) **The guard of F52 was narrowed after the gate of the package.**  The gate of the package of the waves 106 and 107 refuted the claim of the wave 101: the widened guard read the installed dependencies of the plugin (74 MB in `plugin/yeah-provider/node_modules') and refused three files of the code of a dependency -- a refusal with a false subject.  The promise of the claim was not changed: it says «another file OF THE REPOSITORY», and the guard measured more than it promised.  The repair narrows the measurement to the promise: the guard asks git which directories the repository ignores and does not walk them, and it refuses with a named reason when git cannot answer.  The price is named: a rule of the life of a process that hides in an installed dependency is not seen.  The repair and its measurements are in the section 16.105 of `docs/PLAN.md'.
note: The wave is the repair of four defects of the evidence, and every part of it was measured.  (1) **F48 -- the stand of the life.**  The fifth part of `tests/checks/check-a-process-that-is-dead-is-dead-everywhere.el' replaces the reader of the state (`yeah-proc-state', through `cl-letf' and `symbol-function') with a table of the stand: the zombie 999999999 answers `"Z"', the living process 999999998 answers `"S"'.  The rule of the kernel (`yeah-proc-alive-p') stays under the proof and gives its verdict.  Measured: 5a -- `yeah-life-socket-sweep' takes away the socket of the zombie owner (`yeah-life-sweep-999999999.sock') and does not touch the socket of the living owner; 5b -- `yeah-life-adopt' does not refuse the socket of the zombie owner (it takes the socket to itself, the file is in place); 5c -- `yeah-life-adopt' refuses the socket of the living owner with the words "belongs to a living process", and the socket of the living owner stays in place after the refusal.  The host is not asked: the pid of the stand is above the limit of the kernel, and the state is replaced.  The stand writes only into its own temporary directory (mode 0700) and deletes it; the servers it opens are stopped, `yeah-life--owned' is restored.  Controls: F48a -- the honest tree is green (the code 0); F48b -- the mutation of `lib/yeah-life.el' (the owner is always alive) makes the stand fall with its own refusals (the code 1) and the parts 1 to 4 do not fall; F48c -- the registered control of the claim (`sed 's|(or (string= state "S")|(or t|' lib/yeah-proc.el') makes the check fall with seven refusals (the code 1).  (2) **F51 -- the stands of the tree.**  The stands 8, 9 and 10 were added to `tests/checks/check-the-tree-of-the-processes-survives-a-vanished-process.sh'.  Stand 8 -- "the tree is read once": the counter is made *outside* the tree under test, the shell of the stand traces itself with `set -x'; one scan of the tree reads the stat file of every process of the tree exactly once, and the number of the traced lines `read_stat <pid>' equals the number of the scans -- the expectation is **1**.  Stand 9 -- "the tree is stopped as a whole": a real tree of the processes of the host is built (root, `a' with its group and `b' in the group of `a', `c' with its group), it is stopped with `stop_tree <root> TERM', and after that *every* process of the tree (b, a, c, root) must catch the signal; the preconditions are checked explicitly (`process_group'), and if the group is not the one, the stand says "the tree is not measured" instead of being silent.  Stand 10 -- the preconditions of the two.  `scripts/lib/tree.sh' was not changed: both values are measured from outside, through the existing seam `PROC_ROOT', with no stub and no counter in the shared code.  (3) **F52 -- the guard of the rule of the life.**  The third part of the check reads the code of the whole tree (the extensions `el', `sh', `ts', `mjs', `js') through `directory-files-recursively' (the C level): a walk of its own called a function of Elisp for every file, the interpreter piled up `lisp-nesting', and it died with `excessive-lisp-nesting (1601)' on a directory of 115 files.  The documents are not read: a document *names* the rule of the life of a process, a program *defines* it.  Two recognitions: the form of the name (extended -- `-alive-p' and an argument that names `pid' or `process') and the sign (a file that reads the state of a process -- `yeah-proc-state', `/proc/...stat', or the word `state' together with the word `pid' -- and holds the letters of life (`"S"', `"R"', `'S', `'R', `S|R') decides the life of a process by itself, whatever its functions are called); the comments of a line are dropped, because a comment defines no rule.  Two exceptions are named in the code: `lib/yeah-proc.el' (the rule itself) and the check of the wave 101 (the stand of the rule).  Measured: on the honest tree the sign fires on exactly two files -- the rule itself and the stand of the rule -- and there is no false firing (the code 0, 1.0 s).  Controls: F52b (a forgery in `tests/support/yeah-fake-life-rule.el', a name that is not the form of the rule, in a directory that is not the one) is caught by the sign; F52c (a forgery in `scripts/lib/yeah-fake-alive.sh', a shell function that reads `/proc/$pid/stat' and holds `"S"') is caught by the sign; F52d (a forgery in `tests/support/yeah-fake-alive.el' without the letters of life, so that the sign does not fire) is caught by the form of the name; F52e (the two named exceptions taken away in a copy of the tree) gives two refusals, the code 1.  (4) **F53 -- the guard of the records.**  `yeah-check--records' reads `waves/*.json' (110 files).  The rule of a section works for the file that is *named* (the guard looks for the headings of the named file, and that was so in the code before; the records make it visible).  The rule of the file does not apply to the records: a record is a document of the past, it names the files of the day of its wave, and a file that has moved or is gone since that day is named by the record and is not a defect of the record.  A section is a heading of a document (`*.md'), a program and a record have no sections, and the name of the section is left alone.  Measured: among the 160 references to sections of existing paths in the documents and in the records there is not one to a file that is not `.md' -- the rule of today is not weakened.  Controls: F53a -- the honest tree is green (the code 0, 0.74 s); F53b -- the forgery `waves/wave-999.json' that names `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md' section 2.1 is caught by the refusal of the guard ("docs: wave-999.json: line 4: it names ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md §2.1, and there is no such section"), the code 1; F53c -- the defect of F53 put back in place (the name `§2 (Naming)' becomes `§2.1' in three places of `waves/wave-101.json') is caught in all three places (the lines 4, 45 and 47), the code 1; F53d -- the registered control of the claim (`sed -i '$a The name of a file that is not there: `docs/there-is-no-such-file.md`.' docs/PLAN.md') makes the check fall ("docs: PLAN.md: line 7374: it names docs/there-is-no-such-file.md, and there is no such file"), the code 1.  (5) **The amendments.**  The text of the claim of the wave 101 is amended with the exception of the check that proves the claim of the wave 100 (the text and the falsifier of that claim were amended by the wave 106), and the text, the falsifier and the scope of the claim of the documentation are amended by the parent on 2026-11-21; the id, the requirements, the control, the kind, the phase, the owner and the register of both claims stay as they are.  (6) **What stays open.**  F47 stays open in its part `a': the rule "the stat file of a process is read by one module" is left in `lib/', and the promise of the claim of the wave 101 names the exception instead of closing the rule.
